approach:
Add one reading check, `check_part_coverage(reading, request)`, as one new `step!(check_part_coverage(reading, request));` line placed last in `refusing_check`, so no existing refusing case changes its first refuser. `is_bullet` and `request_text_acceptance` stay untouched; a new parser `request_parts` in topics.rs reads numbered parts `(N)`, `N.`, `N)` (runs 1,2,3.. of at least two) and the dash or star bullets of the Acceptance section (all bullets when no opener exists). Quoted or backticked spans, fenced blocks, `>` lines, generated lines and everything after `## Source` are never read as markers (a length-preserving mask finds markers; the item text is then cut from the original line with the quote characters stripped, so a backticked word in a bullet stays in its stems). Criteria, summary and other reading text are tokenised whole, with quoted spans kept (finding 6).

COVERAGE (findings 2, 5, 6). An item is covered by either route. (i) MARKER CITATION, deterministic: a criterion that names the part's marker (`(3)`, `part 3`, `item 3`, with a digit boundary) covers that part whatever the stems, unless that criterion itself has a deferral phrase (so '(3) is left for a follow-up job' does not cover). The refusal message tells the reader to start the criterion with the marker, e.g. `(3): a unit test checks the --json flag output`, the way `Consumers:` repairs another check. (ii) STEM FALLBACK for unnumbered bullets and for uncited parts: the item's own distinctive stems (stems also found in a sibling item are removed; all stems when none remain) must share min(2, ceil(n/2)) stems with one criterion. Items with no stem are not checked. Distinctive stem order, written in a code comment: lowercase token of letters or digits; if longer than 4 chars and ending in s, drop the s; reject if shorter than 4; reject if the raw or singular word is in the stop list (checked BEFORE the cut); cut to 5 chars. The stop list holds domain words (test, tests, pass, passes, change, changes, described, existing, job, part, request, fmt, made, make) AND English function words of 4+ letters, listed in the comment: with, that, from, each, when, into, only, this, then, than, they, them, have, will, would, should, which, there, their, these, those, also, such, some, same, more, most, must, does, been, being, both, over, under, once, after, before, about, other, used, uses, using, need, needs, where, what. The unit test pins 'with', 'that', 'from', 'changes', 'described', 'existing', 'tests', 'pass' as not distinctive, 'clippy' and 'cover' as distinctive, and 'default' = 'defaults'.

DEFERRAL (finding 4). Searched in summary, assumptions, departures and out_of_scope; never in criteria (a criterion may describe the gate). Clauses are cut on `;` and `,`. A clause defers an item when it has a deferral phrase (follow-up, deferred, later job, separate job, not in this job, left for), no negation guard (never, without, refus, unless, do not, not defer), and names the item by marker or by the required own-stem overlap. In summary, assumptions and departures a clause with earlier, previous, previously, prior, last, was, were, had, already or a job id is skipped, so a retry reading that recounts an earlier split is not refused. An out_of_scope item counts for an item ONLY when it has the deferral phrase naming it (same rules, no past guard), or when it is the whole part: the bare marker (`(3)`, `part 3`, `item 3`, optional punctuation) or an item whose every distinctive stem is already a stem of that part and which shares the required overlap, so it restates the part and adds nothing. An item that narrows a covered part ('(2): the web view is unchanged', 'Part 3 beyond the CLI test') adds a stem the part lacks and does not count.

SPLIT EXEMPTION (findings 3 of rounds 1-2). The exemption reads only plain request sentences (not quoted, fenced or generated), per clause (cut on `;` and `,`). A clause permits a split only when it has a modal (may, can, could, might, is allowed to), no negation (not, never, cannot, n't, no), no complaint word (earlier, previous, last, rejected, wrong, said, reading, attempt, bug), and one of two shapes. Shape A: a move verb (split, move, defer, leave, handle, ship, land, deliver, do), at most 4 object words with no path- or identifier-like token (a `.`, `/` or `::`), a preposition (in, into, as, to, for), then a destination that carries a SPLIT SIGNAL: an optional determiner that is only `a`/`an` or none (the determiners this, the, one and same BLOCK), then either an adjective from {separate, follow-up, later, next, another, own} before job(s)/change(s)/PR(s)/pull request(s)/request(s), or a plural noun with a count adjective (several, multiple). A bare noun such as 'the change', 'one PR', 'a change to the parser' has no split signal and never matches. Shape B: a marker or part word (`(3)`, `part 3`, `item N`, `the rest`) as subject of be or become, then `a`/`an`/none, then follow-up, separate, later or another, then job, change or PR. A permitting clause naming markers exempts only those parts; one naming none exempts every item.

FIXTURES (findings 1, 9 of round 2). The fake reader (fake.rs:311) and the CLI Scenario reader (athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs:572-573) return a reading that ignores the request, so the production gate (reading.rs:722) would refuse CLI tests that queue bullet requests. fake.rs adds one marker-stripped content criterion per request bullet or numbered line (cap 300 chars). The real reason for stripping the marker is that the fake producer and verifier split criteria on '. ' with a digit prefix (fake.rs:328-338, 391-394), so a copied `3. text` line would be mis-split; stripping does NOT protect against check_scope_limit, which reads a limit from the criterion's words (checks.rs:705-715, change_limit), so a copied bullet like 'Only src/a.rs may change' is still refused by it, with or without a marker. That is the correct gate behavior (a real reader would repair with `the deliverables`), so the fake does not try to hide it; the end-to-end corpus test includes one such request and pins Refuse(check_scope_limit) as the documented limit of the fake. common/mod.rs is not a listed deliverable; it is the one-seam fix (a helper plus one call in the Reader branch), the smallest way to keep criterion 8 true, and is declared in files and open_questions. The reader brief gets no new rule (briefs.rs and briefs/reader.rs stay unchanged); the refusal message carries the repair.
